subject.title: Plugin install doesn't build native bindings — plugins with better-sqlite3 fail on Node 24 (ABI v137) with bindings file not found

question: Should managed npm plugin installs keep lifecycle scripts disabled and add an explicit trusted native-addon repair path, or should OpenClaw automatically rebuild native dependencies during install?
rationale: The observed failure is valid, but the direct repair changes whether OpenClaw executes plugin dependency build scripts during install, which is a security boundary and product trust-model choice.

options.title: Guarded Doctor/Fix rebuild
options.body: Keep --ignore-scripts as the default, detect missing native artifacts or known native packages, and offer an explicit trusted rebuild or doctor repair path with tests.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Warn or fail with actionable rebuild guidance and leave native addon build responsibility to plugin publishers or operators.

options.title: Automatic rebuild
options.body: Run a targeted npm rebuild during managed plugin install and accept broader install-time code execution for native dependency compatibility.

recommendation.title: Guarded Doctor/Fix rebuild
recommendation.body: Keep --ignore-scripts as the default, detect missing native artifacts or known native packages, and offer an explicit trusted rebuild or doctor repair path with tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history ties both the plugin install surface and the script-suppression hardening to steipete-authored commits.
